reference: Present Simple — tempo verbal base do inglês
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PRESENT SIMPLE: O Present Simple expressa hábitos, fatos e rotinas. Forma: sujeito + verbo (base form). 3ª pessoa singular: adiciona -s/-es/-ies. Exemplos: 'I work every day' (Eu trabalho todo dia), 'She works at a hospital' (Ela trabalha num hospital). Negação: 'I don't work', 'She doesn't work'. Interrogação: 'Do you work?', 'Does she work?'. Usos: hábitos (I drink coffee every morning), fatos gerais (Water boils at 100°C), horários (The train leaves at 8). Advérbios de frequência: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never — ANTES do verbo principal. ERRO COMUM PT: 'I am work' → CORRETO: 'I work'. Nível: A1

reference: Present Continuous — ações em andamento agora
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PRESENT CONTINUOUS: Expressa ações acontecendo AGORA ou planos futuros próximos. Forma: sujeito + am/is/are + verbo-ing. Exemplos: 'I am working now' (Estou trabalhando agora), 'She is studying' (Ela está estudando). Negação: 'I am not working', 'She isn't studying'. Interrogação: 'Are you working?', 'Is she studying?'. Usos: ação em andamento (I'm reading a book right now), plano futuro (I'm meeting John tomorrow), situação temporária (She's living in London this month). Verbos NÃO usados no continuous: know, believe, understand, like, love, hate, want, need, have (posse), belong — são stative verbs. ERRO COMUM: 'I am knowing' → CORRETO: 'I know'. Nível: A1

reference: Past Simple — ações concluídas no passado
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PAST SIMPLE: Expressa ações concluídas no passado. Forma: verbo + -ed (regulares) ou forma irregular. Exemplos: 'I worked yesterday' (Trabalhei ontem), 'She went to Paris' (Ela foi a Paris). Negação: 'I didn't work', 'She didn't go'. Interrogação: 'Did you work?', 'Did she go?'. Marcadores temporais: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2020. Regras de ortografia: double consonant (stopped), y→ied (studied), e→ed (lived). ERROS COMUNS PT: 'I didn't went' → CORRETO: 'I didn't go'; 'She did went' → 'She went'. ATENÇÃO: verbos irregulares NÃO seguem regra — devem ser memorizados. Nível: A2

reference: Present Perfect — passado com conexão ao presente
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PRESENT PERFECT: Conecta passado ao presente — ação passada com resultado/importância agora. Forma: sujeito + have/has + past participle. Exemplos: 'I have visited Paris' ( Já visitei Paris), 'She has lived here since 2020' (Ela mora aqui desde 2020). Negação: 'I haven't visited', 'She hasn't lived'. Interrogação: 'Have you visited?', 'Has she lived?'. Usos: experiência (Have you been to Japan? — alguma vez na vida), resultado presente (I've lost my keys — e ainda não encontrei), ação contínua (She's worked here for 5 years). Marcadores: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for. DIFERENÇA PT→EN: 'Eu já visitei' ≠ 'I already visited' (Past Simple) → Use Present Perfect: 'I have already visited'. Nível: B1

reference: Past Continuous — ações em andamento no passado
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PAST CONTINUOUS: Ações em andamento num momento específico do passado. Forma: sujeito + was/were + verbo-ing. Exemplos: 'I was working at 8 PM' (Estava trabalhando às 20h), 'They were sleeping when I arrived' (Estavam dormindo quando cheguei). Negação: 'I wasn't working', 'They weren't sleeping'. Interrogação: 'Were you working?', 'Was she sleeping?'. Usos: ação interrompida (I was reading when the phone rang), duas ações simultâneas (While I was cooking, she was studying), cena de fundo (It was raining and people were running). COMBINADO COM PAST SIMPLE: 'While I was walking (ação longa), I saw a friend (ação curta)'. Nível: A2

reference: Future: Will vs Going To — intenções vs planos
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — FUTURE: WILL vs GOING TO. WILL: decisão momentânea, promessa, previsão sem evidência. 'I'll help you!' (Vou te ajudar — decisão agora), 'It will rain tomorrow' (previsão sem evidência). GOING TO: plano/intenção, previsão com evidência. 'I'm going to study medicine' (intenção), 'Look at those clouds — it's going to rain' (evidência presente). FORMAS: will + verbo (I will go), am/is/are going to + verbo (I am going to go). Negação: won't, isn't/aren't going to. ERRO COMUM: 'I will going to' → ERRADO — use um OU outro. 'I'll go' = decisão agora; 'I'm going to go' = plano prévio. Nível: A2

GRAMÁTICA EN — CONDITIONALS: 4 tipos. ZERO CONDITIONAL (fato geral): If + present, present. 'If you heat ice, it melts' (Se aquecer gelo, derrete). FIRST CONDITIONAL (possível): If + present, will + base. 'If it rains, I will stay home' (Se chover, ficarei em casa). SECOND CONDITIONAL (hipotético presente): If + past, would + base. 'If I had money, I would travel' (Se eu tivesse dinheiro, viajaria). THIRD CONDITIONAL (hipotético passado): If + past perfect, would have + past participle. 'If I had studied, I would have passed' (Se eu tivesse estudado, teria passado). ERROS COMUNS PT: 'If I will go' → 'If I go'; 'If I would have' → 'If I had'. MISTED CONDITIONAL: 'If I had studied, I would pass now' (passado → presente). Nível: B1-B2

reference: Passive Voice — voz passiva em inglês
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PASSIVE VOICE: Foco no objeto/receptor da ação, não no agente. Forma: sujeito + be + past participle. Present: 'The book is written in English' (O livro é escrito em inglês). Past: 'The letter was sent yesterday' (A carta foi enviada ontem). Future: 'The project will be completed' (O projeto será concluído). Present Perfect: 'The car has been repaired' (O carro foi consertado). Modals: 'The work must be done' (O trabalho deve ser feito). Agente: 'by + agente' (opcional): 'The painting was stolen by a thief'. QUANDO USAR: foco no resultado, agente desconhecido ou irrelevante, formalidade. QUANDO EVITAR: textos claros e diretos — prefira active voice. TRANSFORMAÇÃO: Active 'Shakespeare wrote Hamlet' → Passive 'Hamlet was written by Shakespeare'. Nível: B1

reference: Articles — a, an, the, zero article
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — ARTICLES: A/AN (indefinido): referência não específica, primeira menção. 'I bought a book' (comprei um livro). 'She is an engineer' ( Ela é engenheira). AN antes de vogal sound: 'an hour' (h mudo), 'an MBA' (em-be-a). THE (definido): referência específica, já mencionado, único. 'The book I bought' (o livro que comprei). 'The sun' (sol = único). ZERO ARTICLE: generalizações. 'Dogs are loyal' (Cães são leais), 'Water is essential' (Água é essencial). REGRAS: países → sem artigo (France), EXCEÇÕES: the USA, the UK, the Netherlands. instrumentos: 'I play the piano'. refeições: 'I had breakfast' (sem artigo). ERROS COMUNS PT: 'The Brazil is big' → 'Brazil is big'; 'I am doctor' → 'I am a doctor'; 'She works in bank' → 'She works in a bank'. Nível: A1-A2

reference: Prepositions — in, on, at, by, with, for, to, from
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PREPOSITIONS: IN: meses (in January), anos (in 2024), estações (in summer), períodos (in the morning), lugares fechados (in the room), cidades/países (in London). ON: dias (on Monday), datas (on July 4th), superfícies (on the table), ruas (on Main Street), transporte público (on the bus). AT: horas (at 3 PM), momentos específicos (at night, at noon), endereços completos (at 123 Main St), eventos (at the party). BY: limite de tempo (by Friday), meio/transporte (by car, by plane), agente passiva (by Shakespeare). WITH: companhia (with friends), instrumento (cut with a knife). FOR: propósito (for sale), duração (for 3 years), destino (leave for Paris). TO: direção (go to school), destinatário (give it to me). FROM: origem (from Brazil), distância (2km from here). ERROS COMUNS: 'in Monday' → 'on Monday'; 'at night' ≠ 'in the night'. Nível: A1-B1

reference: Modal Verbs — can, could, may, might, must, should, would
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — MODAL VERBS: CAN: habilidade (I can swim) e permissão informal (Can I go?). COULD: habilidade passada (I could swim when I was 5), possibilidade (It could rain), pedido educado (Could you help me?). MAY: permissão formal (May I speak?), possibilidade (It may rain). MIGHT: possibilidade menor (It might rain — 30-40%). MUST: obrigação forte (You must wear a seatbelt), dedução (She must be tired — certeza lógica). SHOULD: conselho (You should sleep more), expectativa (She should arrive soon). WOULD: condicional (I would go if I could), pedido educado (Would you like some tea?), passado habitual (I would play there as a child). REGRAS: modais NÃO têm -s, -ing, -ed; seguidos de verbo base (sem to). 'She can swims' → 'She can swim'. Negação: modal + not → can't, couldn't, mustn't (proibição), shouldn't. Nível: A2-B1

GRAMÁTICA EN — COMPARATIVES & SUPERLATIVES: COMPARATIVO: adjetivo curto + -er + than (taller than), more + adjetivo longo + than (more beautiful than). 'She is taller than me' (Ela é mais alta que eu). 'This book is more interesting than that one' (Este livro é mais interessante). SUPERLATIVO: the + adjetivo curto + -est (the tallest), the most + adjetivo longo (the most beautiful). 'She is the tallest in the class' (Ela é a mais alta da turma). IRREGULARES: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → farther/further → the farthest/furthest; little → less → the least. IGUALDADE: as + adjetivo + as (She is as tall as me). INFERIORIDADE: less + adjetivo + than (This is less expensive than that). ERROS COMUNS: 'more easier' → 'easier'; 'the most biggest' → 'the biggest'. Nível: A2

reference: Relative Clauses — who, which, that, whose, where, when
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — RELATIVE CLAUSES: Defining (essencial, sem vírgula): 'The woman WHO lives here is a doctor' (A mulher que mora aqui é médica). 'The book WHICH I bought is great' (O livro que comprei é ótimo). THAT pode substituir who/which em defining clauses: 'The woman THAT lives here'. Non-defining (extra, com vírgula): 'My sister, WHO lives in Paris, is a doctor' (Minha irmã, que mora em Paris, é médica). NÃO usa THAT em non-defining! Outros pronomes: WHOSE (posse): 'The man WHOSE car was stolen'. WHERE (lugar): 'The city WHERE I was born'. WHEN (tempo): 'The day WHEN we met'. WHOM (objeto formal): 'The person TO WHOM I spoke'. ERROS COMUNS: 'The woman which lives here' → 'The woman who lives here'; 'The book who I read' → 'The book which/that I read'. Nível: B1

reference: Gerunds & Infinitives — when to use -ing vs to + verb
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — GERUNDS & INFINITIVES: GERUND (verb + -ing): AFTER prepositions (I'm good at swimming), AFTER certain verbs (enjoy, mind, suggest, avoid, finish, keep, practice, consider, imagine, deny, give up), AS subject (Swimming is healthy), AFTER phrasal verbs (I gave up smoking), AFTER 'be worth'/'be busy'/'spend time'. 'He enjoys playing soccer' ≠ 'He enjoys to play' (ERRADO). INFINITIVE (to + verb): AFTER certain verbs (want, need, decide, plan, hope, agree, refuse, offer, promise, learn, expect, pretend, seem), AFTER adjectives (It's important to study), AFTER nouns (I have something to say), AFTER question words (I don't know what to do). VERBS WITH BOTH (diferença de significado): remember + ing (lembro de ter feito) vs remember + to (lembrar de fazer); stop + ing (parar de fazer) vs stop + to (parar para fazer); try + ing (tentar fazendo) vs try + to (tentar fazer). Nível: B1-B2

reference: Reported Speech — discurso indireto em inglês
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — REPORTED SPEECH: Transformando discurso direto em indireto. SHIFT DE TEMPOS: present → past ('I work' → 'She said she worked'); past → past perfect ('I worked' → 'She said she had worked'); will → would ('I will go' → 'She said she would go'); can → could ('I can help' → 'She said she could help'). PRONOMES: adaptam-se ao contexto ('I' → 'she', 'my' → 'her'). EXPRESSÕES DE TEMPO: today → that day; tomorrow → the next day; yesterday → the day before; here → there; this → that. PERGUNTAS: yes/no → if/whether ('Are you tired?' → 'She asked if I was tired'); wh- → keep wh- word ('Where do you live?' → 'She asked where I lived'). IMPERATIVO → told/asked + to + verb ('Study hard!' → 'She told me to study hard'). NÃO SHIFT se verdade universal: 'Water freezes at 0°C' → 'He said water freezes at 0°C'. Nível: B1-B2

GRAMÁTICA EN — QUESTION TAGS: Frase curta no final para confirmar ou verificar. REGRA: positivo → tag negativo; negativo → tag positivo. 'You are Brazilian, AREN'T you?' (Você é brasileiro, não é?). 'She doesn't like coffee, DOES she?' (Ela não gosta de café, gosta?). PRONOMES: usa o pronome do sujeito (This is nice, ISN'T it?). MODAIS: 'You can swim, CAN'T you?', 'We should go, SHOULDN'T we?'. I AM → AREN'T I? ('I'm right, AREN'T I?'). IMPERATIVO → WILL YOU? ('Close the door, WILL you?'). LET'S → SHALL WE? ('Let's go, SHALL we?'). INTONAÇÃO: descendente = confirmação (You're coming, aren't you? ✓); ascendente = pergunta real (You're coming, aren't you? 🤔). ERROS COMUNS PT: 'You are tired, no?' → 'You are tired, AREN'T you?'. Nível: A2-B1

reference: Countable & Uncountable Nouns — contáveis e incontáveis
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — COUNTABLE & UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS: COUNTABLE: podem ser contados (one book, two books). Plural: books. Artigo: a/an + singular. 'I have a book' / 'I have two books'. UNCOUNTABLE: NÃO podem ser contados diretamente (water, rice, information). SEM plural, SEM a/an. 'I have water' (NÃO 'I have a water' NÃO 'waters'). QUANTIFIERS: COUNTABLE: many, few, a few, several, number of. UNCOUNTABLE: much, little, a little, amount of. AMBOS: some, any, a lot of, plenty of. CONTAINERS para uncountable: a cup of coffee, a bottle of water, a piece of advice, a slice of bread, a grain of rice. ERROS COMUNS: 'informations' → 'information' (incontável); 'furnitures' → 'furniture' (incontável); 'advices' → 'advice' (incontável); 'many money' → 'much money'. Nível: A2-B1

reference: Passive in Reported Speech — voz passiva no discurso indireto
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — PASSIVE IN REPORTED SPEECH: Quando o verbo principal é reporting verb e a frase original está na voz passiva. 'They built the house' → 'She said they had built the house' (active). 'The house was built in 1990' → 'She said the house had been built in 1990' (passive). PATTERN: said + that + sujeito + had been + past participle. MODAL PASSIVE: 'The work must be done' → 'She said the work had to be done'. 'The letter can be sent' → 'She said the letter could be sent'. FUTURE PASSIVE: 'The project will be completed' → 'She said the project would be completed'. ERROS COMUNS: esquecer o 'been' ('had built' → 'had been built'); manter modal sem shift ('must be' → 'had to be'). Nível: B2

reference: Conjunctions — connecting words: and, but, or, so, because, although
text: GRAMÁTICA EN — CONJUNCTIONS: AND (e): adiciona ideia — 'I like coffee AND tea'. BUT (mas): contraste — 'She is rich BUT unhappy'. OR (ou): alternativa — 'Do you want tea OR coffee?'. SO (então/portanto): resultado — 'It was raining, SO I stayed home'. BECAUSE (porque): motivo — 'I stayed home BECAUSE it was raining'. ALTHOUGH/THOUGH (embora): contraste surpreendente — 'ALTHOUGH it was raining, we went out'. WHILE (enquanto): simultaneidade ou contraste — 'WHILE I was studying, she was sleeping'. WHEREAS (enquanto/ao passo que): contraste — 'He is tall WHEREAS she is short'. UNLESS (a menos que): condição negativa — 'I won't go UNLESS you come too'. SINCE (já que/desde): motivo ou tempo — 'SINCE you're here, help me'. ONCE (uma vez que): condição — 'ONCE you learn it, it's easy'. ERRO COMUM PT: 'although...but' → ERRADO — use apenas um! 'Although it rained, we went out' ✓ / 'It rained, but we went out' ✓. Nível: A2-B1
